issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename, not the first character of the package name
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path is /Packages/<name-initial>/<nevra>/, where the initial is the first letter of the package name. For typical NEVRA filenames (e.g. 'glibc-2.39-1.fc40.x86_64.rpm') the first character coincides, but for names beginning with digits or punctuation this divergence becomes a silent 404. State the invariant: nevra[0] must equal name[0]. Extract the name explicitly.

issues.description: Silent None return from extract_arch_from_url propagates into a malformed URL
issues.detail: When the regex finds no arch, the function returns None, and the caller concatenates it into the path via f-string, producing '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. There is no termination guarantee on the well-formedness of the output. Either raise an exception or filter; do not let an unhandled None flow into a URL the build system will fetch.

issues.description: Architecture list is hardcoded and duplicated from implicit knowledge elsewhere in the tool
issues.detail: The arches ['x86_64','aarch64','ppc64le','s390x'] are a fact about the project that lives in at least one other place. Centralize the list so a future arch addition is a single-point change, and document why this whitelist exists rather than parsing the NEVRA suffix directly (which would be more robust since arch is the token before '.rpm').

issues.description: Parsing the arch by regex over the whole URL is less rigorous than parsing the NEVRA suffix
issues.detail: The NEVRA filename already ends in '.<arch>.rpm'; that is the authoritative source. Searching the entire URL with \b boundaries works today but admits ambiguity (e.g. a future mirror path containing 'x86_64' would shadow a 'noarch' package). Split nevra on '.' and take the token before 'rpm'. State the invariant once; do not re-derive it from path text.

issues.description: Docstring does not state the invariant or the race condition the function relies on
issues.detail: Literate-programming-grade comment is missing. The function's correctness depends on an external invariant: coreos-koji-tagger will eventually tag the NEVRA into coreos-pool. That assumption belongs in the docstring with a pointer to the dnf5 issue and to the bump-lockfile workflow, so a future reader understands why a URL is constructed before the artifact is reachable.

issues.description: noarch packages may not be handled by the arch whitelist
issues.detail: Fedora repos serve noarch RPMs whose filenames end in '.noarch.rpm' and whose URL path typically contains 'noarch'. The whitelist excludes 'noarch', so extract_arch_from_url returns None for them and the URL becomes '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. Confirm whether noarch URLs ever reach use_koji_url_only via repoquery's --arch noarch path; if so, include 'noarch' or branch accordingly.

review.summary: The patch is small and the algorithm is clear: rewrite any non-coreos-pool URL into the canonical koji /Packages/<initial>/<nevra>/ form. Correctness rests on two unstated invariants, both worth auditing. First, nevra[0] is treated as the package-name initial; this is true only when the filename begins with the same character as the name, which is usually but not always so. Second, extract_arch_from_url can return None, and that None is concatenated into a URL without any check. The arch should be read from the NEVRA suffix rather than searched across the URL, and the external race-condition assumption (koji tag will follow) deserves a literate comment rather than living only in the commit message. UNDER-AUDITED — likely correct in practice, but the invariants are not stated and one None-return path is unhandled.
